subject: Architecture
title: Burj Khalifa: The World's Tallest Tower
description: A fast breakdown of Burj Khalifa: The World's Tallest Tower for builders.

hook.text: The Burj Khalifa stands 2,717 feet tall — over half a mile. It's visible from 60 miles away.

buildup.text: Its Y-shaped floor plan resists wind from all directions, like a tripod standing firm in a storm.

discovery.text: Workers poured concrete at night because daytime desert heat would crack it before it set properly.

twist.text: Dubai nearly went bankrupt during construction. Abu Dhabi bailed it out — and got the tower renamed.

climax.text: The Burj has the world's highest occupied floor, highest swimming pool, and highest observation deck.

punchline.text: Half a mile tall. Built at night. Named after a bailout.

quiz.question: Why was concrete poured at night during Burj Khalifa construction?
options: Desert heat would crack the concrete before it set
Nighttime labor costs were lower in Dubai
